status: conceptual development proposal; no geometry, frame timing or rendered QA
canonicalDieIdentity: Names and six face values are bound in mathematics/configuration.json. Color is redundant with name and visible numbers.
firstFrameContract: Four inspectable unusual dice, mental choice and higher-number rule. First seconds must communicate choosing order without implying certain victory; no logo, greeting, title-card delay or one unexplained winning throw.
opportunitySpace: Each of six face indices on one die combines with six face indices on the other. Same displayed numbers can occur on different equally likely faces. A36-opportunity space is a mathematical model, not36played trials.
simplePair: Keep yellow3 as the constant comparator; reveal four losing orange2faces and two winning orange6faces. Four of six faces conveys the yellow2/3advantage without showing36tinycells.

greenAgainstBlue.representation: A single possibility area divides into18pairs with green5 and18pairs with green1. First18allwin. Second18divide into6againstblue0whichwin and12againstblue4whichlose. The winning union is18+6=24of36.
greenAgainstBlue.continuity: Blue's same4/0face distribution survives the camera/object transition; green's two face groups are equal because both have three faces.
greenAgainstBlue.prohibition: Do not make the four value combinations(5,4),(5,0),(1,4),(1,0)equal-sized/equiprobable; their weights are12,6,12,6. Do not count unique number labels instead of face indices.

orangeAgainstGreen.representation: One third of the possibility area is orange6against any green face:12pairsallwin. Two thirds is orange2:24pairs split into12againstgreen1whichwin and12againstgreen5whichlose. Winning union12+12=24of36.
orangeAgainstGreen.continuity: Green's same three1s/three5s survive; orange's four2s/two6s reappear unchanged.
orangeAgainstGreen.prohibition: Do not make orange's2and6branches equal-sized. No2beats5or1beats4outcome.

circle.arrowMeaning: Counter-choice: starting from a selected die, follow the arrow to the informed reply with2/3winningprobabilityagainstit.
circle.prohibition: These response arrows run opposite to winner-to-loser dominance arrows. Never label them beats or silently switch meanings. State counter-choice visibly; keep the proof ledger's favored-pair names separate.

possibleLoss: A highlighted yellow3versusorange6is a possible outcome with yellow losing despite its2/3advantage. Mark illustrative possible outcome; never claim a random sample, playback of a real game or empirical proof.
cubeTruth: Actual future cube topology/face allocation must use a valid six-face net and preserve labels across all visible rotations. No guessed standard opposite-face sums, impossible net, changing face values or certification of physically fair dice.
endingContract: The same die paired against different opponents makes the final matchup dependence visible; settle the circle instead of adding a generic follow/comment/outro.
laterColdViewerQuestions: Can an unfamiliar viewer state what wins and why the second chooser can respond advantageously?
Can they explain why yellow usually beats orange without saying3beats6?
Can they explain each mixed case without interpreting four value categories as equally likely?
Can they follow the response arrows without reversing who has favorable odds?
Do they understand that no die is universally strongest here and any favorable roll can still lose?
inspectionLimits: Conceptual reasoning only. No human panel, video/audio, cube model, animation, mobile preview, caption plan, native device test or audience effect observed.
